cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

A minimum of 5 years of experience in analysis, interpretation and application of financial and accounting policies, practices and procedures (preferably in higher education or public sector settings); or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience with Oracle Cloud, Concur, and Cognos or similar software

The Financial Services Analyst 3 serves as the Business Resource Center's (BRC) subject-matter expert in one or more core financial service areas, including but not limited to: bank card administration, recharge billing, payment card platform administration, UCOP fiscal close activities. This role reviews and approves financial transactions submitted by UCOP departments and resolves complex financial service issues. Additionally, this role skillfully interprets UC policies and applies UCOP procedures, translating complex requirements into practical, understandable guidance that supports sound decision-making, addresses regulatory compliance and manages risk across BRC operations.
Business travel and entertainment reimbursement audit
Bank card administration support
Recharge billing, expense/cost transfers, and financial journals
Account review and management, including appropriations and expenditures analysis
Signature delegation management - Web page and SharePoint support
Illumia (formerly Transact/CashNet) administration, including building and maintaining storefronts, reconciliation, and PCI compliance
UCOP fiscal close activities
Audit of financial transactions and procedures within the BRC
Financial and other ad hoc reporting and analyses for varied and complex financial transactions

Analyzes, skillfully interprets, and applies UC policies to UCOP procedures. Translates complex policy requirements into practical, understandable guidance that supports sound decision-making, addresses regulatory compliance and manages risk.
Reviews and approves financial data and transactions submitted by UCOP departments, ensuring accuracy
Documents procedures for financial activities and creates training materials for client departments
Proficiency with MS Office and standard desktop/web-based applications and databases; willingness to learn new software and technologies.

Manages up effectively: Actively supports manager’s priorities and objectives; Communicates proactively to avoid surprises on status, risks, or deadlines; Builds and maintains trust through reliable follow-through; Anticipates leadership's information needs and exercises judgment on when to escalate
Service Excellence as a Core Value: responsive to client requests, builds client relationships, and anticipates client needs.
Works independently and stays accountable: Uses job and team resources effectively; Analyzes problems independently; Takes responsibility for problem resolution and seeks counsel appropriately.
Attentive to detail, with an eye for how tasks fit into the bigger picture.

Strong interpersonal skills, analytical skills, service orientation, active listening, critical thinking, attention to detail, ability to multi-task in a high volume environment, organizational skills, effective verbal and written communication skills, sound judgment and decision making; ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.

Excellent working knowledge in at least one of the following areas: general accounting, recharge billing, travel and entertainment reimbursement rules, or auditing of financial procedures/transactions.
Working knowledge of UC business systems, account structures, encumbrances, expenditures, and related policies and procedures or the ability to quickly acquire it.

Strong analytical skills: identifies key factors, patterns, and trends; interprets policy; synthesizes information from multiple sources (policy, financial reports, statistical data); meticulous attention to detail.

Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain moderate-to-complex issues clearly and concisely, compose professional business correspondence, and actively listen to clarify key points.

Strong interpersonal skills: collaborates effectively across teams and levels, maintains composure in sensitive situations, and provides guidance, coaching, and mentoring to staff. Collaborative team member who supports colleagues, including assignments that aren't your own. Awareness of and respect for how your work and presence impacts the team.
Strong organizational skills: independently prioritizes workload, manages high volumes of work with frequent interruptions, and tracks competing deadlines.
